messages:
maria: Heads-up — prototype for a lightweight heuristic admission flow + golden-bench integration landed on feat/admit-lite. I want alignment on acceptance signals before I flip the flag.
kevin: link to PR?
anna: grabbing it now. quick thought: bench vs runtime mismatch is our usual footgun — kv-cache warmups and batching change token distribution.
raj: agree. we should separate signals: 1) perf safety (latency/cpu/gpu), 2) correctness safety (gold prompt delta), 3) stability signals (errors/tracebacks). each with independent abort rules.
sara: can we tag telemetry early? something like `admit.source=heuristic, admit.bucket=golden-v1` so we can slice quickly.
bench-bot: quick run summary for feat/admit-lite on golden-v1: p50=19ms, p95=48ms, p99=110ms, error_rate=0.12%, quality_delta=+0.3% (n=150). full logs: https://ci/internal/bench/6172023456
kevin: bench numbers look fine but p99 110ms is higher than our normal baseline (85ms). what's the seqlen distribution on that run?
bench-bot: seqlen percentiles: 50=32, 90=120, 99=384. workload includes long completion tails.
anna: that's the point — golden set skewed long. if runtime traffic is shorter we might be fine, but we need to test with sampled runtime traces. also quantized kernels can amplify p99.
raj: proposal: add a two-way check before acceptance: (A) golden-bench pass with tolerances (delta_quality >= -1% and error_rate < 0.5%), (B) runtime-smoke on sampled live traces with p99_latency_increase < 30% and error_rate delta < 0.2%. both must pass.
maria: I like that. can we encode the thresholds in the admit config so ops can tune without code changes? e.g.:
```
admit_policy:
  golden_min_quality_delta: -1.0
  golden_max_error_rate: 0.5
  runtime_max_p99_rel: 1.3
  runtime_max_error_delta: 0.2
  canary_fraction: 0.01
  canary_duration_hours: 24
```
kevin: yes. also add a hard rollback on any crash loop or nvcc kernel OOMs. those should abort immediately.
sara: and ensure we emit `admit.phase` tags (golden/run/canary) and `admit.variant` so cost dashboards can split.
onboard-bot: FYI — model registry will mark model state=admit-pending when PR includes `admit_policy` block.
anna: edge-case: quantized models sometimes pass golden but fail runtime due to FP fallback on kernels — add a quick hybrid runtime that forces quant path to catch that.
maria: good call. raj — can you own adding the runtime trace sampler and the smoke harness? kevin — can you add the abort-on-kernel-oom detector? i'll update the PR with the admit_policy config and a canary runbook.
raj: yep, I'll add sampler + smoke harness. plan: 1% trace replay, preserve kv prefix lengths, run over 3h sliding window, produce p50/p95/p99 + quality on golden prompts cross-check.
kevin: will add detector and a short deploy hook that watches `nvcc/oom` logs + GPU mem spikes.
sara: i'll add the telemetry tags and a couple grafana panels for quick triage (admit.*).
maria: plan sounds good. i'll stub the checklist in the PR and schedule a 30m follow-up tomorrow to sign off. ping me when PR updated. :thumbsup:
kevin: pinged on the PR once updated.
anna: thanks — also adding a note to include sequence-length stratified golden buckets so we don't get surprised by long-tail regressions.
maria: noted — adding bucketization and a required sample size per bucket (n>=50) to the golden check. i'll update the config and canary playbook tonight.
